name: ReadModel
summary: Load the particle content, amplitudes and parameters of a model for use throughout HEPCAT.

syntaxes.description: Read the numbered model files from a directory.

details: Start a calculation by reading a model once and giving the resulting value a name, for example `qedModel = ReadModel[modelDirectory, 2]`. Pass that value to [CreateDiagrams](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/CreateDiagrams), [ConstructAmplitude](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/ConstructAmplitude) and the other model-dependent functions. You can keep several models in the same Mathematica session.

The first argument is the directory containing the model tables; the second is the number in their filenames. A constructive model numbered `2` uses `prtcls2.mdl`, `amps2.mdl`, `vars2.mdl` and `func2.mdl`. The returned list is `{particles, amplitudes, variables, functions}`. Usually you can pass it on unchanged rather than unpacking its tables.

Particle names in a process are strings from that model, including their case and helicity suffixes. In the bundled QED model, `"e"` and `"E"` are the electron and its antiparticle, while `"A.+"` and `"A.-"` select photon helicities. HEPCAT numbers legs by their positions in the process list and takes all external momenta as ingoing.

examples.description: Read the bundled QED three-point model and see its four sections.
Retrieve a mass and its locally resolved numerical value.

detail_sections.title: Choosing the right amplitudes for a calculation
paragraphs: The model used to draw diagrams supplies the allowed interactions. A separate model used for [FactorizationAmplitudeChannels](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/FactorizationAmplitudeChannels) must supply complete lower-point amplitudes. A five-point factorization channel can contain a complete four-point amplitude, so a list containing only three-point vertices is not sufficient for that purpose.

For the bundled QED examples, model `2` supplies the three-point vertices. Model `3` also contains known higher-point amplitudes and is used as factorization input for the larger examples. The required information is determined by the process, not by a special meaning attached to the numbers `2` and `3`.

An amplitude absent from the factorization model is treated as zero. Check that the model contains the lower-point results you intend to use; HEPCAT cannot distinguish an intentionally zero amplitude from one that has not yet been entered. [AppendModelAmplitudes](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/AppendModelAmplitudes) adds already established results to a constructive model.

detail_sections.title: Parameters and Feynman models
paragraphs: Masses and couplings remain symbolic [ModelParameter](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/ModelParameter) objects belonging to this model. Reading a model does not assign numerical values to global names such as `Me` or `EE`. Use [ModelParameterRules](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/ModelParameterRules) when you want numerical substitutions or local overrides.

A directory containing `lgrngN.mdl` but no `ampsN.mdl` is read as a CalcHEP Feynman model. The result has the head [FeynmanModel](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/FeynmanModel), allowing the same diagram-generation interface to choose Feynman rules. Its bare vertices are not a replacement for complete lower-point amplitudes in constructive factorization.
Missing files, malformed expressions and unterminated tables return `Failure`. Inspect that result before continuing; a failed read is not an empty or zero model.

name: ReadVariables
summary: Inspect the independent parameter table of a model file.

syntaxes.description: Return the variable rows in a numbered varsN.mdl file.

details: For ordinary calculations, use [ReadModel](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/ReadModel). `ReadVariables[file]` is useful when you are inspecting or building a model and need its independent parameters without loading the other tables. Give the complete filename, such as `vars2.mdl`.

The result is a list of `{parameter, value, comment}` rows. Each parameter is represented by a model-local [ModelParameter](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/ModelParameter), so reading the file does not set global Mathematica values. Use [ModelParameterName](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/ModelParameterName) to read its name as a string.

These rows are declarations, not a complete numerical substitution scheme. [ModelParameterRules](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/ModelParameterRules) works on the complete model and also resolves dependent definitions and overrides. Use it when evaluating an amplitude numerically.
The table must end with its normal separator. Malformed parameter names or expressions return `Failure`, rather than running code from the file.

examples.description: Inspect one declared variable.
List the declared names rather than assigning them.

name: ReadFunctions
summary: Inspect a model file containing dependent parameter definitions.

syntaxes.description: Return the rows of a funcN.mdl table.

details: Use this reader when examining how a model defines derived quantities, such as a coupling calculated from other input parameters. The first argument is a complete `funcN.mdl` filename. [ReadModel](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/ReadModel) normally reads this table for you.

Each returned row retains the model-local parameter, its defining expression and its comment. Reading a definition does not assign it to a global symbol and does not numerically resolve all of its dependencies. To obtain usable numerical substitutions for the complete model, call [ModelParameterRules](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/ModelParameterRules).

A function supplied by an external model is stored as [ModelFunction](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/ModelFunction) data. HEPCAT does not run an unrelated Mathematica function merely because it has the same printed name. Unresolved definitions can therefore remain symbolic while other, supported definitions are still usable.

examples.description: Inspect the QED dependent definitions.
Resolve the complete model locally.

name: ReadParticles
summary: Inspect the particles, antiparticles, spins and masses declared in a model file.

syntaxes.description: Read the eleven-column prtclsN.mdl table.

details: Supply the complete `prtclsN.mdl` filename. The result is the particle table used by [ReadModel](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/ReadModel). You usually do not need this separate reader unless you are inspecting or constructing a model.

A row contains the full name, particle and antiparticle names, particle identifier, twice the spin, mass, width, color information, auxiliary information and two display names. Process lists use the particle-name strings, not the full descriptive names or newly created Mathematica symbols.

The mass column can contain a model-local [ModelParameter](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/ModelParameter). [ParticleMass](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/ParticleMass) retrieves it without requiring you to remember the column number. The twice-spin and particle identities also let HEPCAT distinguish boson and fermion exchange symmetry; equal numerical masses do not make two species identical.

examples.description: Read the particle table.
Find the electron mass from the particle declarations.

name: ParticleMass
summary: Find the mass declared for a particle or antiparticle.

syntaxes.description: Return the mass declared for a particle name.

details: The first argument is a model particle name such as `"e"`. The second is the particle table, normally `model[[1]]`, rather than the complete model. Both the particle name and its antiparticle name are recognized.

The answer is the mass as declared in the model. If it is a [ModelParameter](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/ModelParameter), it remains symbolic until you apply [ModelParameterRules](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/ModelParameterRules). This lets the same expression be used with more than one numerical parameter choice.

The empty name `""`, used as padding in model tables, gives `0`. An unknown nonempty name gives `-1`. When accepting a process supplied by someone else, check for that value rather than interpreting it as a physical mass.

examples.description: Particle and antiparticle have the declared common mass.
examples.input:
qedModel = ReadModel[modelDirectory, 2];
ParticleMass["e", qedModel[[1]]] === ParticleMass["E", qedModel[[1]]]

name: ReadAmplitudes
summary: Inspect the complete constructive amplitudes stored in a model file.

syntaxes.description: Read an ampsN.mdl table using the particle declarations for spin and mass information.

details: For routine use, load the complete model with [ReadModel](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/ReadModel). This separate reader takes an `ampsN.mdl` filename and the matching particle table. It is useful when inspecting the amplitude part of a model or checking newly written rows.

Each row contains the external particle names, any empty padding columns, an overall factor and an amplitude expression divided by that factor. Multiply the last two entries to recover the full stored amplitude. The reader translates the model file's bracket notation into [SpinorChain](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/SpinorChain) and other typed HEPCAT expressions.

Reading does not complete a list of helicities, derive missing amplitudes or establish that the stored expressions are correct. Unlisted lower-point amplitudes are treated as zero by [FactorizationAmplitudeChannels](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/FactorizationAmplitudeChannels). Validate results before adding them with [AppendModelAmplitudes](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/AppendModelAmplitudes).

examples.description: Read the QED vertex-amplitude rows explicitly.
Recover the complete expression in one row.

name: ConvertAmplitude
summary: Convert a constructive model row from text into typed spinor notation.

syntaxes.description: Convert the final amplitude string using the row's external particles.
Use an explicit parameter scope for model data.

details: The row has particle-name columns followed by an overall factor and an amplitude string. The return value is the converted final expression; the separate overall factor is not multiplied into it.
Compact angle and square brackets become SpinorChain expressions. Interior digits become momentum insertions; the particle table selects massive "Spin" or massless "Helicity" endpoints.
The converter recognizes x factors, propagator denominators and declared model parameters. For example, s13-Me^2 represents PropDen[Mom[Multiparticle[1,3]], Me] with the model-local mass parameter.
Compact bracket digits are single-digit labels. Use typed SpinorChain, Spinor and Mom expressions when multi-digit external labels or more explicit structures are required.
The current converter uses the restricted model expression parser. ConvertAmplitudeOld is retained for historical compatibility and is not the recommended model reader.

examples.description: Translate a massive angle bracket from a three-point row.
Convert a photon square bracket in a four-point row.

name: ConvertAmplitudeOld
summary: Access the historical string converter retained for compatibility.

syntaxes.description: Use the older string-replacement converter; new code should use ConvertAmplitude.

details: This historical implementation predates the model-local parameter parser. Its original spinor-type setup is no longer active in the function, so it is not a supported replacement for the current row-based converter.
The old implementation uses general string replacement and expression conversion. Do not use it to import arbitrary model text or rely on it for multi-digit labels.
For new work, load an entire model with ReadModel or call ConvertAmplitude with a full row and particle table.

examples.description: A scalar constant is a minimal compatibility example.
Use the current converter for a typed amplitude.

name: AddOppositeHelicityAmplitudes
summary: Mechanically add angle-square conjugate rows with reversed massless helicities.

syntaxes.description: Retain each row and add its helicity-reversed bracket partner when applicable.

details: For a row containing particle names ending in .+ or .-, the added row reverses all of those suffixes, interchanges angle and square spinors, and interchanges xFactor with xTildeFactor. The separate factor is retained.

This is a mechanical model-building operation, not a proof of a model's parity properties or coupling conjugation conventions. Verify the resulting amplitude and normalization for the theory being entered.
ReadAmplitudes does not currently call this operation automatically. Explicitly listed helicity amplitudes remain the clearest way to specify a complete model.

examples.description: Inspect the two helicity names in a small row pair.
Inspect the converted square-bracket partner.

name: AppendModelAmplitudes
summary: Add established amplitude expressions to a constructive model for later factorization calculations.

syntaxes.description: Append {particles, amplitude} or {particles, factor, amplitudeOverFactor} entries to ampsN.mdl.

details: Use this function after obtaining and checking a new amplitude. For example, once a five-point result has been established, storing it in a model makes it available when [FactorizationAmplitudeChannels](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/FactorizationAmplitudeChannels) builds six-point channels. The function writes the expressions you supply; it does not derive or validate their physics.

Give the target directory, model number and a list of entries. An entry `{particles, amplitude}` writes the complete expression. The longer form `{particles, factor, amplitudeOverFactor}` separates a common overall factor from the expression stored after it. The particle list uses the same all-ingoing order and names as the expression.

The target model supplies the particle declarations and parameter names. When taking a result from a different model, replace its model-local [ModelParameter](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/ModelParameter) objects with the corresponding parameters of the target model before writing. Matching printed names do not by themselves merge the two parameter scopes.

The result reports the destination file and the numbers of added and skipped entries. An identical existing entry is skipped. A conflicting expression for the same particle multiset rejects the batch instead of silently replacing the old result. Every proposed row must be readable again before the amplitude file is replaced.

Existing rows and comments are preserved. Reload with [ReadModel](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/ReadModel) to use the new data. First try a temporary copy of a model, as in the example, and use [CheckAmplitudes](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/CheckAmplitudes) and any independent comparisons appropriate to the process before promoting a result to factorization input.

examples.description: Append a known four-point result to a temporary copy of the three-point QED model.
An empty batch leaves the target untouched and reports zero additions.

name: ModelParameter
summary: Refer to a mass, coupling or other parameter belonging to a particular model.

syntaxes.description: Find a declared parameter by its string name.
Retain a parameter as inert model-local data.

details: Use `ModelParameter[model, "Me"]` to retrieve the model's declaration of the parameter named `Me`. It prints with that familiar name, but it is an inert object carrying the identity of its model. This is why two loaded models can both contain `Me` without changing one another.

Keep these objects in symbolic amplitude expressions. Apply [ModelParameterRules](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/ModelParameterRules) to obtain numerical values, optionally with different values for selected inputs. Assigning a value to an unrelated global symbol called `Me` does not change a model-local parameter.

The three-argument form is the representation stored by the model reader: a name, a scope and a domain. Most users should retrieve parameters from [ReadModel](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/ReadModel) rather than manufacture that representation. The `"Real"` domain makes the parameter unchanged by complex conjugation.

A name lookup that is missing or ambiguous returns `Failure`. It does not create a new declaration. Use [ModelParameterName](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/ModelParameterName) when you need the string name, for example to match parameters while transferring an amplitude between models.

examples.description: Retrieve a declared electron mass.
Override a value locally without assigning Me globally.

name: ModelFunction
summary: Keep a model-supplied external function as symbolic data.

syntaxes.description: Represent an external function belonging to a model.

details: Some model tables refer to a function implemented by the model's numerical environment, for example a running-mass prescription. [ReadModel](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/ReadModel) keeps such a call as `ModelFunction[name, scope, arguments]` instead of evaluating an arbitrary Mathematica function with the same name.
The scope identifies the model and the final list contains the arguments. Usually this object appears as part of a dependent parameter definition rather than something you need to construct by hand.

A retained function call can be used in symbolic work, but its numerical value is not automatically available. [ModelParameterRules](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/ModelParameterRules) resolves supported arithmetic and dependencies; unsupported external calls remain unresolved. Supply appropriate declared inputs or a supported numerical prescription before relying on checks that require that quantity.

examples.description: Inspect an inert call without invoking a global function.
Convert the retained call to model-style text.

name: ModelParameterName
summary: Return the string name of a model-local parameter.

syntaxes.description: Extract the name from a ModelParameter reference.

details: Use this when reporting parameters or matching their names between two models. For example, the parameter returned by `ModelParameter[model, "Me"]` has the name `"Me"` even though the complete object also carries a model scope and a domain.

The result is a string, not an assignable Mathematica symbol and not a numerical value. To obtain numerical replacement rules, use [ModelParameterRules](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/ModelParameterRules). To retrieve a parameter in another model, pass the returned name to [ModelParameter](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/ModelParameter).

examples.description: Read a declared parameter name.
List the names that resolved to numerical parameter values.

name: ModelParameterRules
summary: Obtain numerical parameter substitutions while keeping model definitions local.

syntaxes.description: Resolve model variables and supported dependent functions.
Apply local overrides keyed by ModelParameter references or string names.

details: Apply the resulting rules to a symbolic expression when you want numbers. The model itself and any global Mathematica names are left unchanged. Independent input parameters and the supported dependent definitions are resolved together.

The optional second argument changes selected inputs for this calculation. It can use model-local [ModelParameter](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/ModelParameter) references or string names, for example `{"Me" -> 1}`. Dependent definitions are then recomputed, so changing an input remains consistent with quantities derived from it.

An explicit override of a dependent parameter treats that value as an independent input for this evaluation. This is useful for a numerical comparison, but you are responsible for whether that parameter choice describes the intended theory.

A dependency cycle or an unsupported [ModelFunction](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/ModelFunction) call cannot always be given a number. Such unresolved definitions are omitted while unrelated resolvable parameters are retained. Inspect the rules if a later numerical calculation reports a parameter without a value.

[CheckAmplitudes](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/CheckAmplitudes), [CompleteFactorization](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/CompleteFactorization) and [ConstructAmplitude](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/ConstructAmplitude) normally obtain numerical values from the model themselves. You do not need to repeat its defaults in every call.

examples.description: Resolve the bundled QED numerical parameters.
Replay a calculation at unit mass and charge locally.

name: FactorizationPartitions
summary: Enumerate distinct complementary external-leg partitions for tree factorization.

syntaxes.description: Partition numbered external particles into two sides containing at least two external legs each.

details: External legs are tagged by their original positions, so two identical particles remain distinct numbered legs. A partition and its complement are included only once.
The output enumerates possible cuts before asking whether the supplied model supports a nonzero intermediate species and two nonzero lower-point amplitudes.
FactorizationAmplitudeChannels performs the model-dependent sewing. These partitions are combinatorial input and should not be summed as amplitudes.

examples.description: There are three distinct two-sided partitions at four points.
The five-point combinatorial partitions number ten.

name: LookupAmplitude
summary: Retrieve a stored lower-point amplitude with a specified particle numbering.

syntaxes.description: Match particle names, multiply the stored factor, and relabel typed particle slots.

details: This is an advanced way to obtain a complete amplitude already present in a constructive model. `taggedParticles` has entries such as `{"e", 1}` and `{"E", 2}`. The function matches their particle content to a stored model row, includes that row's overall factor and relabels its typed particle slots to the supplied numbering.

Only particle-label positions are relabeled. Numerical coefficients, powers and independent spin-index symbols are not interpreted as particle numbers. Repeated identical species are assigned distinct matching labels instead of repeatedly replacing every occurrence by the same leg.

The `rightSide` argument and four supplied spin-index names support sewing lower-point amplitudes across an internal line. In an ordinary lookup with only integer external labels, the common form is `LookupAmplitude[Thread[{particles, Range[Length[particles]]}], model, False, {i1, i2, i3, i4}]`.

An absent amplitude returns `0`. That is the same missing-amplitude convention used by [FactorizationAmplitudeChannels](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/FactorizationAmplitudeChannels). For an entire calculation, prefer that function or [ConstructAmplitude](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/ConstructAmplitude), which also carry the channel and external-state information needed for sewing and validation.

examples.description: Retrieve the QED positive-helicity three-point amplitude.
examples.input:
qedModel = ReadModel[modelDirectory, 2];
LookupAmplitude[{{"e", 1}, {"E", 2}, {"A.+", 3}}, qedModel, False, {i1, i2, i3, i4}]

examples.description: Missing model amplitudes give zero.
examples.input:
qedModel = ReadModel[modelDirectory, 2];
LookupAmplitude[{{"e", 1}, {"e", 2}, {"e", 3}}, qedModel, False, {i1, i2, i3, i4}]

name: FactorizationAmplitudeChannels
summary: Build the known lower-point amplitude products that a full amplitude must reproduce at its physical poles.

syntaxes.description: Return the nonzero channel products for the specified all-ingoing process.

details: Give an ordered, all-ingoing process list and a constructive model containing the required lower-point amplitudes. A channel divides the external legs into two groups. When the momentum flowing between those groups goes on shell, the full amplitude must factor into the corresponding two lower-point amplitudes, with the internal states sewn together.

The return value is a compact list, one row per nonzero channel. A row has the form `{m1, ..., mn, Multiparticle[cut], exchangedMass, expression}`. The first entries are the external masses in process order; the cut lists the momenta that sum to the internal momentum. The final entry is the sewn product with its propagator denominator and the historical `1/z` factor.

You can inspect these rows directly, but you normally pass the list unchanged to [CheckAmplitudes](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/CheckAmplitudes) or [CompleteFactorization](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/CompleteFactorization). Those functions interpret the channel information and sewing convention. Do not remove `z`, fit an overall sign or simply sum the channel expressions to make a candidate full amplitude.

Colored channels sew the internal color indices as well as the internal spin state. The expression therefore retains the same explicit SU(3) tensors as [DiagramAmplitudes](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/DiagramAmplitudes). This is important when photon, gluon and weak exchange contribute to the same reaction: their color tensors interfere differently. Missing or ambiguous color information is not replaced by an overall multiplicity.

Use higher-point model data for a five-point factorization.

detail_sections.title: Supplying enough lower-point information
paragraphs: For four-point factorization, the lower amplitudes have three legs. At five points, a channel can involve a three-point and a complete four-point amplitude. At six points, complete four- and five-point amplitudes can be needed. The diagram model can still contain only the allowed vertices; the factorization model serves a different purpose.

The bundled QED model `2` supplies three-point vertices. Model `3` also stores known complete amplitudes for larger channels. Use [ReadModel](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/ReadModel) to load the model appropriate to the multiplicity you are checking.

An unlisted lower-point amplitude is treated as zero and does not produce a nonzero channel row. The user is responsible for supplying all known nonzero lower-point amplitudes. A CalcHEP [FeynmanModel](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/FeynmanModel) contains bare vertices, so it is not accepted as the factorization model.

detail_sections.title: Preparation and interpretation
paragraphs: A sewn channel product is already valid before optional algebraic simplification. For large expressions, the final ordinary simplification attempt has a short finite budget. A timeout retains the complete original product, including every propagator and regular term, rather than delaying the whole channel inventory indefinitely. Small channel expressions keep the established simplification path. No internal on-shell assumption is added by this performance safeguard.

Massless three-point kinematics has two complex branches: either the angle brackets vanish or the square brackets vanish. A helicity amplitude can be supported on only one branch. Sewing keeps that information from the original lower-point factors, before canceling ratios that could otherwise turn an unsupported 0/0 expression into a nonzero answer.

At four points, two contributions supported on different exhaustive branches can use one common continuation when an exact symbolic external-spinor identity proves that it represents both. They are not counted twice, summed blindly or averaged. Two lower factors requiring incompatible branches have no generic single-cut contribution. The returned channel rows retain their ordinary compact format.

[PrepareAmplitudes](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/PrepareAmplitudes) can simplify channel rows without changing their compact format. Such a row declares only its selected internal cut; it does not put every other propagator in the product on shell. Request preparation details if you will pass those reductions to completion, so the original channel targets remain available.

Different channels overlap on multiple poles. Adding their products as independent diagrams would generally double count those overlaps. [CompleteFactorization](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/CompleteFactorization) instead solves the channel conditions together, starting from the diagram expression and a bounded space of possible corrections.

name: CreateDiagrams
summary: Generate the tree diagrams allowed by a model for an ordered external process.

syntaxes.description: Generate trees for an ordered all-ingoing external particle list.
Use the equivalent separate-particle argument form.

details: The process is a list of model particle-name strings. Their positions fix labels `1`, `2`, and so on, and all external momenta are ingoing. For example, `{"e", "E", "A.+", "A.-"}` selects two fermion states and two photon helicities in the bundled QED model.

The result is a list of diagram objects, not an amplitude sum. Use [CreateArrowDiagrams](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/CreateArrowDiagrams) to draw them. Use [DiagramAmplitudes](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/DiagramAmplitudes) to obtain one mass-rule/expression pair for each diagram, then [PrepareAmplitudes](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/PrepareAmplitudes) to simplify those expressions.

For constructive models, each generic internal photon or gluon represents the combined helicity contribution. It is not necessary to generate a separate topology for each internal helicity. The model's particle, antiparticle and twice-spin declarations also determine fermion connections and exchange signs.

With a [FeynmanModel](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/FeynmanModel), the same call selects Feynman vertices and propagators. Those internal numerators remain off shell. [FeynmanToSpinorProducts](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/FeynmanToSpinorProducts) or Feynman preparation converts their Lorentz and Dirac structures for comparison.

This function generates diagrams from the supplied interactions. It does not infer missing vertices, complete an amplitude from factorization data or establish that a simplified sum passes physical checks. [ConstructAmplitude](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/ConstructAmplitude) combines those later stages when you want the full workflow.

Generate all six photon orderings at five points.

name: CreateArrowDiagram
summary: Draw one tree diagram and optionally inspect its vertex and propagator expressions.

syntaxes.description: Draw one diagram returned by CreateDiagrams.
Optionally display the vertex and propagator expressions.

details: Pass one diagram returned by [CreateDiagrams](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/CreateDiagrams), for example `First[diagrams]`. The drawing shows numbered external legs, internal connections and particle labels, so you can relate the topology to the symbolic amplitude.

The default drawing emphasizes the particle structure. Set `"ShowVertexExpressions" -> True` to display the expressions at its vertices, or `"ShowPropagatorExpressions" -> True` to display its propagators. These options change the drawing, not the diagram data or its amplitude.
To draw the complete list with the same display choices, use [CreateArrowDiagrams](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/CreateArrowDiagrams).

examples.description: Draw the first QED tree.
Inspect its expressions as well as its topology.

name: CreateArrowDiagrams
summary: Draw all the diagrams generated for a process.

syntaxes.description: Draw a list returned by CreateDiagrams.
Apply diagram display options to every tree.

details: This is the usual display companion to [CreateDiagrams](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/CreateDiagrams). Store the generated list in `diagrams`, then evaluate `CreateArrowDiagrams[diagrams]` to see the individual tree topologies.
The order corresponds to the input list. The drawings help you identify which external momenta form each internal line, but they do not combine or simplify the amplitude expressions.

The options of [CreateArrowDiagram](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/CreateArrowDiagram) are applied to every drawing. Turn on vertex or propagator expressions when investigating a particular construction; leave them off for a compact overview.

examples.description: Display both QED four-point diagrams.
Include propagator expressions.

name: diagramAmplitude
summary: Evaluate the expression associated with one generated diagram.

syntaxes.description: Return one diagram's bare amplitude expression.

details: This lower-level singular function returns only the expression. For a process, use DiagramAmplitudes, which retains each diagram's mass rules with its expression.
Constructive evaluation combines internal photon or gluon helicities and expands external x factors. Known mass replacements are applied before return.
Feynman evaluation retains ordered Dirac chains, Lorentz and color tensors, and off-shell internal lines. Convert Feynman tensors through the dedicated Feynman tools or preparation workflow.
A single diagram generally is neither reference independent nor a complete amplitude. Its simplification may need completion after diagrams are combined.

examples.description: Inspect the first constructive diagram expression.
Prefer the mass-rule pair when continuing to preparation.

name: DiagramAmplitudes
summary: Obtain a symbolic amplitude expression and its mass replacements for each generated diagram.

syntaxes.description: Return {{massRules, expression}, ...} for the generated diagrams.

details: Pass the complete list returned by [CreateDiagrams](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/CreateDiagrams). The result is `{{massRules, expression}, ...}`, with one entry per diagram. This format keeps the expression next to the mass information needed when preparing it.

Each mass list declares the external particle masses and, for a constructive diagram, its internal-line masses. Known mass replacements are applied to the expression and retained in the list. In particular, the declarations identify which internal numerator relations are available to [PrepareAmplitudes](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/PrepareAmplitudes).

Constructive diagrams combine the internal photon or gluon helicities and replace supported external x factors before returning. Use the plural function for the full process: some simplifications and pairings involve the diagram list rather than an isolated diagram.

For Feynman diagrams, the result retains Dirac chains, Lorentz or color tensors and off-shell propagators. Their mass lists contain external masses only; no internal on-shell condition is declared. Use Feynman preparation or [FeynmanToSpinorProducts](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/FeynmanToSpinorProducts) before comparing their spinor expressions.

This is the diagram result before factorization and high-energy completion. For constructive work, simplify it diagram by diagram first and keep preparation details if you want the discarded remainders available to [CompleteFactorization](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/CompleteFactorization). Use [CheckAmplitudes](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/CheckAmplitudes) to assess a proposed complete sum.

For a constructive model with colored particles, each diagram retains its explicit [ColorDelta](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/ColorDelta), [ColorGenerator](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/ColorGenerator) or [ColorStructure](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/ColorStructure) tensor. Color is attached before internal helicities are combined. Two helicity contributions are combined only when their color tensors agree. Supported unique SU(3) invariants follow from the particle table and the cubic spinor amplitude; an ambiguous interaction returns Failure instead of guessing a color factor.

examples.description: Get the two separately declared four-point diagram expressions.
Prepare them with a physical-pole preference.

name: DiagramAmplitudeRecords
summary: Inspect the expression, propagators and assumptions associated with each diagram.

syntaxes.description: Build a record for each generated diagram without adding an automatic shell reduction.

details: This is an advanced inspection tool for a list returned by [CreateDiagrams](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/CreateDiagrams). It returns one association per diagram, keeping its original expression, numerator, physical propagators, external particles and mass rules together.

details: Near a simple pole with denominator `t`, an amplitude has the form `R/t + regular terms`. Its residue coefficient is the finite limit of `t` times the amplitude at `t = 0`. Each channel is an association specifying its `"Cut"`, `"Complement"`, `"Mass"` and `"ExternalLegs"`. A physical cut changes momenta, spinors and propagators together. Merely replacing one occurrence of [PropDen](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/PropDen) by zero is not enough to evaluate a spinor expression consistently.

Without a coherent `"KinematicMap"`, the result is labeled `"FORMAL"`: it can identify the coefficient of opaque propagator symbols, but does not certify a physical residue. For ordinary model-based comparisons, [CheckAmplitudes](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/CheckAmplitudes) builds its supported coherent kinematic samples for you.

A custom map `f[expression, channels, poleVariables]` must evaluate every momentum, spinor and denominator in a common chart near the requested cuts. `"KinematicKind"` distinguishes sampled from symbolic charts. Singular or incompatible restrictions are reported rather than interpreted as zero.

The optional structural coefficient is included by default. Set `"StructuralCoefficient" -> False` to skip that extra opaque-propagator calculation when you only need the mapped result. That option does not loosen the kinematic checks.

syntaxes.description: Run the combined checks and return a compact status table.

details: Give the proposed amplitude, the ordinary channel rows from [FactorizationAmplitudeChannels](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/FactorizationAmplitudeChannels), and the constructive model used for those channels. The amplitude may be a bare expression, one `{externalMassRules, expression}` pair or a list of diagram pairs to be summed.

The default result is a compact table of checks. `PASS` means that the requested comparison succeeded at the recorded samples. `FAIL` is a disagreement. `Opp Sign` means a residue or full-amplitude comparison agrees after an overall sign reversal; the expressions are left unchanged. Opposite signs require investigation before these amplitudes are used together in factorization. One isolated amplitude comparison does not establish a consistent convention for the whole model. `UNRESOLVED` means the requested calculation could not establish a result, for example because a form is unsupported or a time limit was reached.

The function reports what the supplied expression does. It does not change a sign, fit a normalization, simplify away a discrepancy by a new internal-shell assumption or repair the amplitude. To determine corrections from the known channels, use [CompleteFactorization](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/CompleteFactorization).

An amplitude with explicit SU(3) color tensors is checked in an exact independent color basis, with a Color column identifying each coefficient in the report. The coefficients are tested separately rather than treating a sum of different tensors as one scalar amplitude. External mass metadata and the supplied model must determine the colored representations; ambiguous metadata returns Failure. For a full numerical comparison, [WriteSPINASProcess](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/WriteSPINASProcess) retains the interference between those coefficients.

For a colored candidate with an optional Feynman benchmark, the independent color basis is built from the candidate, original channel targets and benchmark together. Every coefficient is compared, including a color direction appearing only in the benchmark. Supply "FeynmanModel" for a benchmark read from a different model; its parameters are not borrowed from the constructive model.

detail_sections.title: What is checked
paragraphs: Physical poles are defined by the supplied factorization channels. At each pole, the checker compares the residue of the full amplitude with the sewn product of complete lower-point amplitudes. It accounts for HEPCAT's amplitude and propagator conventions, including the sewing minus sign. Every other propagator is kept away from its pole during an ordinary single-pole comparison.

For an all-massless four-point cut, the exact sample charts cover both valid complex branches. Charts where every Mandelstam invariant vanishes are not used as generic single-pole tests. The expected residue must itself be regular on the selected branch.

Apparent denominator poles not certified as physical by those channels are examined for cancellation. The checker discovers supported angle brackets, square brackets and other inverse factors from the expression. A spurious-pole `PASS` is evidence that the complete amplitude is finite on the tested approach to that apparent pole; individual summands may still diverge and cancel.

The high-energy check increases the energy at fixed scattering angles while holding external masses and couplings fixed. The default bound is the renormalizable tree-level expectation `E^(4-n)` for `n` external particles. If your theory requires another bound, state it with `"HighEnergyBound"`. For supported homogeneous spin tensors, an exactly certified constant rescaling can simplify the spinor basis used by this growth test. The rescaling is independent of energy, so it preserves the growth powers of every component. Details records ConstraintBasisRescaling when used. Residue, reference and Feynman comparisons retain normalized external states.

When explicit Xi reference spinors remain, their choices are varied together while the physical momenta and external spin states are held fixed. An expression without explicit Xi objects has no explicit reference choice left to vary. This check does not claim a separate Ward-identity proof.

detail_sections.title: Inspecting a disagreement
paragraphs: Start with the table to see which kind of check failed. Ask for `"Output" -> "Residues"` to display calculated and expected pole samples, or `"HighEnergy"` and `"References"` to inspect those comparisons. `"Summary"` gives counts; `"Details"` retains the full report, sampled momenta, parameter rules and the actual random seed.

Numerical parameter values come from the model by default. A `"ParameterRules"` list overrides selected inputs locally and recomputes dependent values, without changing the symbolic amplitude. Set an integer `"RandomSeed"` to replay the same sampled comparison.

The checks provide sampled evidence, not a proof that two symbolic expressions are identical for every allowed kinematic point. Increase the sample count or use independent tools when investigating a suspected agreement. The detailed report states which checks and kinematic restrictions were actually completed.

detail_sections.title: Optional comparisons and narrower reports
paragraphs: Use `"FeynmanAmplitudes"` to supply an independently obtained spinor-form Feynman expression or amplitude pairs. The full sums are compared away from propagator poles with no internal-shell substitutions. [FeynmanToSpinorProducts](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/FeynmanToSpinorProducts) and [PrepareAmplitudes](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/PrepareAmplitudes) provide the conversion and ordinary preparation steps.

A Feynman comparison checks every coherent massive-spin coefficient at each requested off-cut sample. A common overall minus remains visible as `Opp Sign`, with `OverallSign -> -1` in its detailed report. The checker does not fit a normalization or change either expression. [ConstructAmplitude](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/ConstructAmplitude) requires strict agreement, so `Opp Sign` prevents a validated result. With color, every independent coefficient must have the same sign: relative sign changes alter interference. Before reusing lower-point amplitudes, align the underlying vertex and external-state conventions across the model rather than flipping individual final formulas.

All four standard categories are enabled by their automatic defaults when applicable. For a deliberately narrower physical-residue-only report, set `"SpuriousPoles" -> {}`, `"HighEnergyCheck" -> False` and `"ReferenceCheck" -> False`. A missing or disabled test must not be interpreted as a successful check of that property.

A colored physical-residue-only report still includes every physical channel and its status. Disabling optional categories removes only those categories; it does not remove the physical comparison rows or their residue samples.

Automatic scheduling takes the number of coherent massive-spin components into account. A short expression can still represent sixteen or more components; those checks can reuse an existing worker pool instead of being treated as a small scalar calculation. Explicit parallel settings and custom kinematic maps keep their usual meaning.

A high-energy PASS can come from an exact conservative bound on every spin component. This route also applies to compact expressions with several massive-spin legs, where separate Laurent expansions would be expensive. The report then says “At most” and records an upper-bound certificate; it does not claim to have measured a leading power.

An inverse bracket between two massless external legs can be included in that bound only if its leading coefficient is exactly nonzero along the sampled high-energy direction. Whether the corresponding spurious pole cancels is checked separately.

name: PrepareAmplitudes
summary: Simplify diagram expressions, factorization channels or a completed amplitude before the next calculation stage.

syntaxes.description: Prepare a mass-rule pair, a list of diagram pairs or compact factorization-channel rows.
Choose and simplify a bounded set of allowed reference-spinor assignments.
Retain original inputs, selected references, discarded remainders and preparation diagnostics.

details: This is the preparation step between generating expressions and completing an amplitude. It contracts spin indices, chooses requested reference spinors, reduces spinor products and tries bounded improving identities. Unlike [CompleteFactorization](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/CompleteFactorization), it does not add missing physical contributions.

Accepted inputs are one `{massRules, expression}` pair, a list of such diagram pairs, or the compact rows returned by [FactorizationAmplitudeChannels](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/FactorizationAmplitudeChannels). The ordinary output keeps the same format. You can inspect one prepared diagram or channel without unpacking a large report.

The mass declarations are part of the meaning of an input. A diagram may declare several internal cuts; a factorization row declares only its selected cut; a completed amplitude should carry external mass rules only. Preparation does not infer new on-shell conditions merely because a denominator appears in the expression.

For a four-leg amplitude, preparation can first keep a channel momentum as one off-shell vector while reducing neighboring external endpoints. For example, using `P=p1+p2=-(p3+p4)` together in several chains can expose a cancellation that disappears when each chain is expanded separately. The pass uses exact affine momentum identities and external Dirac equations, then restores the original momentum labels. It records no internal-shell assumption and preserves each complete denominator product. The rule is structural and also applies to unequal masses, relabeled particles and explicit spin indices.

For small four-leg numerator sums with a declared massless external particle, a bounded Schouten lookahead can inspect an intermediate expression that is temporarily larger. Each candidate is followed by chainwise external Dirac reduction, declared massless momentum factorization and ordinary momentum conservation. This ordering can expose a short result that a strictly greedy one-edit search misses. The original inverse factors are protected throughout, and only a completed, strictly simpler candidate is retained. Detailed output records the Schouten edits and the subsequent identity steps.

For a complete amplitude, preparation can cancel a massless angle- or square-bracket denominator whose invariant factor becomes visible only after terms are combined. It expands numerator propagators by their exact definitions and uses the declared external masses and, when enabled, total momentum conservation. Physical propagator denominators remain off shell. Any nonzero polynomial remainder retains its original bracket denominator, so this pass does not discard regular terms or impose an internal shell condition. The bounded pass keeps the input when it finds no improvement. Standalone [ReduceSpinorProducts](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/ReduceSpinorProducts) still does not infer momentum conservation.

A useful cancellation may require replacing the same momentum in several chains together. For a completed amplitude, preparation therefore revisits small numerator groups that share their complete denominator product, using coherent momentum conservation followed by ordinary spinor reduction. Existing inverse factors stay intact, so the trial cannot impose an internal mass shell. Canonical color coefficients can be simplified separately and reassembled exactly. The whole candidate must improve the existing complexity ranking before it is selected.

Preparation can also simplify scalar coefficients using dependent functions declared in the supplied model, such as a weak mixing relation or a chiral coupling definition. This uses symbolic definitions, not the numerical default values of independent parameters. A propagator's declared mass and width remain unchanged, and equally named parameters from another model remain distinct. A definition is expanded only when the completed expression becomes simpler and the coefficient change has an exact algebraic certificate. Explicit local overrides of dependent parameters in [ConstructAmplitude](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/ConstructAmplitude) are respected.

These are bounded searches for better representations. An unchanged result means that the inspected routes found no improvement within their limits; it does not establish a global minimum. Request `"ReturnDetails" -> True` to inspect accepted reductions and their ordinary-identity routes. Simplifying a saved amplitude also does not replace its physical validation with [CheckAmplitudes](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/CheckAmplitudes).

With `"Parallelization" -> Automatic`, tiny batches stay serial when no HEPCAT worker pool is already available, avoiding startup cost for work that finishes almost immediately. A warm pool can be reused. Substantial batches can still start workers using the available processor allowance, and explicit `True` requests the parallel route. This execution choice does not alter the identity rules or the order of returned items.

For a supported four-leg massive tensor with two spinor endpoints per external leg, preparation also tries a bounded combination of Schouten, external Dirac and momentum-conservation identities. This can remove momentum products or several insertions together even when no single greedy edit improves the expression. It uses the supplied expression and external masses, without a known target amplitude. An optimizer may propose coefficients, but an exact rational replay through the ordinary identities is required before accepting the result. If its proposal identifies monomials that should cancel, a small exact linear solve can enforce those zeros using the same identities. Every cancellation must replay exactly. If that solve fails, the ordinary candidates remain available; no small term is dropped by tolerance. [ConstructAmplitude](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/ConstructAmplitude) uses this optional cleanup on the final fixed expression, after it has built and fitted the correction family. Physical propagator arguments and other kinematic inverse factors remain protected, and the route adds no internal-shell assumption. Unsupported sectors keep the existing route. Detailed output records the accepted identity certificates. Within its shared time budget, the search can revisit a shortened result and compare several reversible choices of external-label frame. This exposes momentum-conservation identities that a single canonical choice can miss. Each accepted endpoint must strictly improve the complete expression and carry its exact replay. Completed amplitudes are tried again after ordinary chain reduction, which can make a previously unsupported long chain eligible. If the complete four-leg expression exceeds the size or momentum-branching guard, preparation can instead group its terms by their original inverse propagator spectators. Each smaller numerator receives the same bounded ordinary identities; its local guards are unchanged. The groups share one finite allowance of up to ten seconds, and an accepted checkpoint must improve the rank of the complete reassembled expression. Exact group reconstruction and inverse-preservation certificates accompany the local identity routes. This changes algebraic grouping, not the amplitude: no internal on-shell condition, process-specific formula or numerical model substitution is introduced.

detail_sections.title: On-shell conditions and protected denominators
paragraphs: [ReduceSpinContractions](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/ReduceSpinContractions) and [ReduceSpinorProducts](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/ReduceSpinorProducts) apply the ordinary contraction and external-particle identities. Preparation additionally knows the complete external leg list and can try momentum-conservation reductions.

Some reductions become shorter only after several identities work together. For a completed amplitude, a bounded endpoint-contraction pass can combine Schouten identities with external Dirac equations, join massless spinor products into a momentum chain, and use declared external momentum conservation to contract the result. Angle and square forms are considered on the same footing. A completed trial is kept only when its whole-expression complexity improves; the diagnostic report records the accepted route. These are ordinary identities, so they do not put any internal propagator on shell. Set `"MomentumConservation" -> False` to exclude the steps that need the complete external momentum sum.

With `"InternalOnShell" -> True`, constructive numerator reductions can use the internal mass declarations belonging to that individual diagram or channel. For example, knowing the mass of the line with momentum `p2+p5` can replace its numerator scalar product `p2.p5` by a combination of masses. The physical [PropDen](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/PropDen) denominators remain off shell.

Such a numerator choice is a representative valid on the declared cut; it need not be an identity away from that cut. Request `"ReturnDetails" -> True` when the result will feed completion. The report retains the original expressions and discarded remainders, giving completion more information than the compact result alone.

A completed `{externalMassRules, expression}` pair has no internal cut declarations, so it can be prepared again using ordinary identities without introducing internal-shell conditions. Feynman preparation also keeps internal numerators off shell and uses one common reference assignment for each external gauge leg across all diagrams.

detail_sections.title: Choosing reference spinors
paragraphs: `"PolePreference" -> Automatic` compares allowed choices and keeps the simplest completed trial within the reference budget. `"AllSpurious"` prefers other eligible massless external particles as references and uses a certified physical momentum-insertion reference for a leg when no spurious choice is available. `"AllPhysical"` uses momentum-insertion references that introduce physical poles outside the constructive item's own cuts. `"Mixed"` compares both types.

`"Cyclic"` and `"ReverseCyclic"` give reproducible massless-particle reference choices. `"Xi"` makes the references common, `"IndependentXi"` keeps a separate generic reference for each external particle, and `None` leaves the supplied references unchanged.

These options express a choice of representation. The search is finite, so a result is not guaranteed to be globally shortest. An unavailable requested choice or an unfinished computation is reported rather than silently treated as fully prepared.

detail_sections.title: Keeping the result and controlling effort
paragraphs: Use the ordinary output for inspection or a short calculation. Use `"ReturnDetails" -> True` when passing preparation information into [CompleteFactorization](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/CompleteFactorization). `"Output" -> "Expression"` returns a bare sum; details preserve the item reports, reference assignments and retained differences.

A final bounded regrouping can shorten the written result without changing its expanded terms or momentum insertions. It groups terms by their existing physical propagators and factors shared spinor coefficients. A regular piece can be combined with an existing pole group when that makes the whole expression smaller. Every accepted rewrite has an exact rational-algebra identity check with the spinor chains treated as independent objects; no additional on-shell or momentum-conservation condition is used, and no new spinor denominator is introduced. This is a presentation improvement, so [SpinorExpressionComplexity](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/SpinorExpressionComplexity) can remain unchanged even when the expression is shorter. The same search can group propagators in two levels, first by a mass class or by whether their channels contain a declared external leg, then by the remaining pole factors. This exposes short exchange-current blocks that can be obscured by one large common denominator. The groups are inferred from the supplied expression; no known amplitude is substituted.

Normal resource settings are automatic. The live display shows progress through the items. Independent diagrams or channels can be prepared in parallel; set `"Parallelization" -> False` to keep the work on the main kernel, or use `"MaxKernels"` to reduce the worker count.

The ranking compares weighted complexity first, expression size second, and additive grouping third. This favors a shorter expression tree when two forms have the same weighted complexity, even if it uses more separate fractions. On eligible completed inputs, a short initial pass also tries ordinary grouping by existing physical poles before heavier exploration; it retains a completed improvement if later optional work reaches its limit. If preparation stops at a limit, inspect its status before assuming all requested reductions were completed. Giving more time permits a larger search but does not prove that a shorter expression exists. [SpinorExpressionComplexity](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/SpinorExpressionComplexity) provides the ranking measure used to compare candidate forms.

details: Start with diagram expressions or their detailed [PrepareAmplitudes](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/PrepareAmplitudes) report, the channels from [FactorizationAmplitudeChannels](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/FactorizationAmplitudeChannels), and the factorization model. With `"PolePreference" -> "AllPhysical"`, the pole check treats finite numerical factors such as `1/Sqrt[2]` as scalar coefficients. Kinematic denominator factors must still be integer powers of propagators supplied by the physical channels.

A successful ordinary result is `{externalMassRules, expression}`. It contains no internal-shell declarations for the complete amplitude and can be passed directly to preparation, [CompleteHighEnergy](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/CompleteHighEnergy) or [CheckAmplitudes](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/CheckAmplitudes). Use `"Output" -> "Expression"` if you specifically want the bare expression.

For a large massive-spin tensor, a short displayed starting expression can still lead to many coupled correction directions. The automatic factorization allowance therefore measures the original channel targets, prepared channel expressions and retained shell or reference source slots before starting the core deadline. Its work estimate also counts the model-consistent parameter assignments that the existing fitter will use. It does not expand the sources or inspect unrelated derivation histories. This estimate changes no correction cap, fit sample count or held-out sample count; explicit stage limits and the overall construction deadline remain authoritative.

detail_sections.title: Why the channels are solved together
paragraphs: A factorization channel determines an amplitude on one pole. Extending its expression away from that pole is not unique, and different channels can share double or higher simultaneous poles. Simply adding a correction for each failed channel can double count a shared contribution or spoil a channel that already passed.

Completion therefore constructs a finite set of correction directions from the supplied information and determines their coefficients using all channel conditions at once. Diagram reweightings, terms retained during preparation and alternative reference choices can supply useful directions. The original lower-point channel products remain the targets throughout.

If the initial physical-pole space is proved inconsistent, Automatic can try a bounded enlargement derived by ordinary external momentum conservation in its numerator sources. Exact rewrite records and a reconstruction of every original direction certify any dependency removed from that enlarged space. Regular remainders stay correlated with their source. This adds no independent contact interaction and does not replace the original channel targets.

Individual correction directions can have higher poles that cancel only in their fitted sum. When an exact rational Laurent expansion is available, completion constrains all higher principal-part coefficients to vanish and fits the finite simple-pole residue at the same time. This retains useful correlated directions without accepting a higher-pole final amplitude or a singular expected target.

The function does not search every imaginable expression and does not invent an unknown interaction. If a required lower-point amplitude is absent from the model, or the available correction directions cannot express a needed contribution, longer fitting alone is not a guarantee of success.

For a small coherent-spin tensor, physical-pole completion first tries a compact correction space from the already reduced channel sources, including ordinary two-particle cuts. This avoids introducing a large collection of redundant coordinates before it is needed. A proposal still has to fit every original channel and pass independent validation; larger tensor systems retain their correlated source route.

detail_sections.title: Retaining information for the following stages
paragraphs: Detailed preparation reports are preferred when simplifying aggressively. They keep the original diagram expressions and the pieces discarded by diagram-local numerator-shell reductions. Completion tries useful retained pieces before constructing broader alternatives, rather than having to rediscover that information from a reduced sum.

Residue agreement can leave combinations of corrections undetermined because they vanish on all tested physical poles. Request `"ReturnDetails" -> True` if the result will go to [CompleteHighEnergy](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/CompleteHighEnergy). That report retains the whole remaining family, not just one chosen expression.

`"PolePreference"` biases the representation searched for: for example, `"AllPhysical"` favors forms with physical denominator poles. It never permits a failed channel to be ignored. Identical-particle exchange symmetry is inferred from the supplied particle identities and model spins when that information is available; `"ExternalParticles"` can provide the process for a bare expression.

detail_sections.title: Validation, limits and failure reports
paragraphs: Coefficients are fitted using coherent kinematic samples and then checked on independent samples. A failed validation point can be added to the equations before another fit. Model numerical values are used for fitting and checking; the returned amplitude retains its symbolic parameters.

Resource settings are automatic by default. `"TimeConstraint"` and `"MaxCorrectionTerms"` can impose explicit limits. `"RandomSeed"` records or repeats the sampling. More time allows more work within the available correction space, not an unrestricted search for a unique answer.

An unfinished result normally returns `Failure["IncompleteAmplitude", ...]` instead of presenting an unchecked candidate as an amplitude. To investigate, request `"ReturnDetails" -> True` and examine the candidate, validation, attempted correction space and remaining free parameters. A successful factorization fit still needs the high-energy, spurious-pole and any independent checks appropriate to the theory; sampled residue agreement alone is not a uniqueness proof.

details: Physical residues do not always determine an amplitude completely. A combination of corrections can vanish on all physical poles while still changing the amplitude elsewhere. This stage uses high-energy growth, spurious-pole cancellation and explicit reference independence to constrain the freedom retained by [CompleteFactorization](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/CompleteFactorization).

Finishing the fitted charts does not finish the calculation: remaining directions still need exact identity classification and the candidate still needs independent checks. For a large tensor with higher-degree massive-spin legs, Automatic reserves finite time for that work when it declares the high-energy and overall construction deadlines. The overall constructor includes a second reserve for its closing validation after the high-energy child returns. This keeps a full child allowance from consuming the time needed by the wrapper's own checks. Neither reserve relaxes a check, reduces sampling or extends an expired call. Explicit deadlines remain unchanged.

For the staged workflow, pass detailed factorization output so the remaining family is available. Passing only one displayed amplitude can lose alternative directions that were present in the fit. An advanced calculation can instead supply a justified `"CorrectionBasis"` explicitly.

Detailed preparation and factorization reports also retain the expressions discarded by diagram-local or channel-local shell reductions. The high-energy stage can fit those source differences before relying on reweighting the prepared pole terms. This matters when the lost piece is regular at a physical pole and is therefore invisible to that residue. The correction must still satisfy every original physical channel, high-energy condition, spurious-pole check and reference test. This does not introduce independent contact interactions into the theory.

When the model has dependent masses or couplings, automatic supplementary parameter assignments vary independent inputs and recompute the declared functions. Explicit local overrides stay fixed. The same correction coefficients are fitted simultaneously across these assignments, so a cancellation that occurs only at the default numerical masses does not masquerade as a symbolic identity. These are additional exact sampled constraints and independent checks, rather than an analytic uniqueness proof.

Reference-independence fitting uses exact rational external on-shell kinematics when available. All massive-spin components remain in the fit, momentum conservation is checked exactly, and no internal propagator is put on shell. This avoids expensive square-root normalization factors in the linear equations. For a large affine family, the constant term and original correction coefficients can be collected before the spin polynomial is expanded. Their reference differences are recombined before equations are extracted, so cancellations between coefficients remain available. The original full-family reference baseline and random assignments stay unchanged. A sufficient exact certificate can prove that every syntactic inverse base is nonzero there; singular or unsupported cases retain the original regularity check. The final candidate still has to pass independent physical-kinematics checks; these fitting samples are not a proof of reference independence at every point.

For a supported four-point process containing a massive Dirac pair, a scalar and a massless vector, automatic completion first tries a minimal cubic-current continuation. The scalar and pseudoscalar couplings are recovered from the model's angle- and square-bracket three-point bilinears and matched symbolically to their Dirac currents. The vector vertex and the original diagram propagators must also match. This bounded first attempt retains the inherited factorization freedom and performs every independent check. If it does not complete, the remaining stage time is used for the broader retained-source fit. A colored current additionally requires an exact rank-one fundamental color-flow projection certificate; its coordinate and any basis phase are preserved.

Detailed output also records ExactDerivativeZeroClassification when a fitted coefficient has an exactly zero rational derivative before the ordinary identity portfolio runs. Its witness is the original solved family, not the final expression after coefficients were set to zero. Any later retained-candidate recovery replays that original derivative and its solution map before combining the certificate with the ordinary identity proofs.

A direction containing auxiliary Xi spinors can be removed only after an ordinary identity proof. The symbolic proof keeps independent coordinates for every reference label, all coherent external spin components and symbolic model parameters. It checks exact rational cancellation with external shells and momentum conservation, without sampling reference values or imposing internal shells.

For a large coherent-spin calculation with failed initial checks, Automatic can first fit a small set of complete shell differences retained by preparation. Each difference keeps its model couplings and correlated terms. This attempt shares the stage deadline and the inherited factorization family; if it does not complete, the full source space remains available. Already-passing inputs skip this proposal, and an explicit correction basis stays authoritative. Detailed output records the proposal and its result. An exact contradiction in the reached equations rejects that proposal immediately; later charts cannot repair it. The report retains the contradiction and identifies charts that were not attempted. Accepted amplitudes still require all requested charts, parameter assignments and independent final checks.

When a large massive-vector identity contains derived model parameters, the exact proof first makes a bounded attempt with those scalar parameters still independent. This stronger ordinary identity can be much easier to prove than an expression with unnecessary square roots from expanded mass relations. Only a complete exact zero certificate removes a direction; a failed attempt retains the original declared-model proof route and the same overall deadline. The numerator identity remains fully symbolic, with no internal on-shell assumption. Rational denominators may be cleared to make that proof cheaper. A separate exact nonzero witness on the same conserved chart certifies the denominator's nonempty generic domain; it is never used as evidence that an amplitude vanishes. This prefix and the declared-model fallback share the original proof deadline. The preferred exact chart can use its existing prefix allowance without another fractional split, which avoids interrupting a complete tensor proof just before it finishes. Large retained vector-source columns can be shortened before fitting by grouping terms with the same original propagators and non-mass couplings. Ordinary spinor identities then see the complete external-mass partners together. Each column keeps its single correction coefficient; its expanded terms are not assigned independent coefficients. Only declared external masses enter this reduction. The original complete columns remain available, and a bounded or unsupported reduction leaves its original column unchanged. The same ordinary grouping can precondition a large vector direction before its exact identity proof. The shorter expression must still receive an exact zero certificate before a coefficient is removed; the full original direction and the reduction steps stay in the report, and an unfinished proof keeps the original fallback. A short tensor-identity attempt can prove a supported four-leg direction zero before those parameter definitions are expanded. It removes a coordinate only when the complete result is literally zero and the exact ordinary-identity route is retained; a lower complexity alone is insufficient.

For a large affine vector family, repeated typed spinor monomials can be expanded once on the same conserved energy chart and recombined through their exact original coefficient map. Every source part is reconstructed exactly, every Laurent coefficient keeps its remainder-order certificate, and all original correction coordinates and constant offsets stay coupled. Exact numerical coefficients are simplified by ordinary algebra before solving, with an exact replay of every replacement. Within one energy chart, completed certified scalar series are reused for identical exact expressions, variables and requested orders. This saves repeated work across monomials without changing their equations. The bounded cache is cleared before the next chart or parameter assignment; failures and approximate inputs are not stored. A failed certificate cannot become a passing equation, and the existing expansion remains available when the bounded shared calculation is unsupported. Supported homogeneous spin tensors also admit constant rescalings of outgoing massive spinor solutions in the energy equations. Removing angular normalization radicals makes the series simpler. Exact entrywise identities and one nonzero, energy-independent factor for the entire affine family certify that every spin component and every forbidden energy power is retained. Physical residues, reference tests and Feynman comparisons use the normalized external states.

Within one energy fit, the exact masses and couplings already requested for that parameter assignment can be inserted before the affine parts and repeated-monomial catalog are expanded. Combining equal coefficients earlier avoids building an unnecessarily large intermediate fit matrix. This changes when those same numerical values are evaluated, not the symbolic amplitude or its correction family. Every original affine coordinate remains coupled. Inexact or nonfinite assignments decline this shared-catalog shortcut. If the catalog detects a parameter or mass rule involving a correction coefficient, energy coordinate or spin coordinate, the caller instead stops the energy fit as UNRESOLVED with a FittingCoordinateCollision diagnostic before whole-family mapping. Details records the local scope in `"FittingParameterSpecialization"`; it does not claim an identity across all parameter assignments. No integer particle labels or unrelated numerical coefficients are replaced globally.

The private scheduling estimate for a catalog scales with its measured work. Details records this soft estimate as `"ChartWorkloadBudget"`, alongside the finite hard allowance `"ChartTimeConstraint"`. Both remain inside the existing high-energy stage and overall construction deadlines; a soft work estimate does not extend either clock or a shorter explicit allowance. This scheduling choice changes no Laurent coverage, fit equations, validation assignments or required checks, and requires no new public option.

If the affine family exceeds the single-catalog size guard, the energy calculation can use blocks of the original correction coordinates. An exact reversible bookkeeping proof reconstructs the whole family from those blocks, with the constant part included once and every coefficient retained in its original order. Each block must complete the same Laurent orders and spin coverage on the same chart. The resulting coefficients keep their original normalization and are added across blocks before the simultaneous solve, so cancellations between different correction coordinates remain available. All blocks share one hard chart deadline and memory bound within the existing stage deadline. No independent block coefficients, extra fit assumptions or public options are introduced; Details retains the block reconstruction and coverage certificates. If a block cannot finish or its reconstruction or coverage certificate fails, the energy fit returns UNRESOLVED with its diagnostic. The same oversized family is not sent back through whole-expression mapping; the original symbolic family and its unfinished obligations remain retained.

For larger spin tensors, the high-energy equations are formed from separate exact scalar Laurent series. The correction coefficients remain coupled in each spin-component equation, including its constant term; they are not tested independently or estimated from a few spin assignments. For supported large tensors, finite Laurent series are used as the coefficient field before the spin polynomial is multiplied out. Their remainder orders and conservative leading-power bounds are retained through every product, so a positive power that later multiplies a negative power is not lost. Every coefficient must cover the requested order before its remainder is removed. The same certified engine supports fitting and the final high-energy check; a bounded unsupported attempt retains the ordinary route, while an unproved scalar-series zero assumption remains unresolved.

After an energy chart fixes some correction coefficients, later charts and model-consistent parameter assignments can use the exact affine family that remains. The first equations stay in their original coordinates, and every later restricted equation is retained alongside them. A reduction is used only when its complete free-coordinate map and every retained equation are verified exactly; otherwise the previous family remains in use. All requested charts, parameter assignments and final independent validation checks are still evaluated.

The ordinary successful output is `{externalMassRules, expression}`. It can be simplified again with [PrepareAmplitudes](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/PrepareAmplitudes), using ordinary external identities only, and checked with [CheckAmplitudes](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/CheckAmplitudes).
