detail_sections.title: The physical conditions
paragraphs: The automatic high-energy bound is `E^(4-n)` for a renormalizable tree amplitude with `n` external particles. The comparison takes fixed-angle high-energy limits while holding masses and couplings fixed. Supply `"HighEnergyBound"` when your theory requires a different stated growth condition.

A proposed correction is also checked against the original physical channels. Removing a spurious singularity or improving energy growth is not allowed to spoil factorization. Explicit Xi references are varied when present, and apparent denominator poles must satisfy the supported cancellation checks.

Only directions supported by the model and the supplied calculation are considered. The function does not create an unrestricted contact-interaction basis or infer new QED interactions. If the stated constraints leave a genuine free interaction, that freedom must remain unresolved rather than being assigned an arbitrary number.

Redundant correction directions are removed only after exact identity proofs. The proof portfolio combines ordinary external reductions with economical massive-spinor coordinates, checking every coherent-spin coefficient. A supported large direction may use the faster coordinate proof first. Angle and square basis choices describe the same complete spin tensor; they are calculation choices, not assumptions that the theory is parity invariant.

When a conservative high-energy certificate already establishes the requested bound for every component, expensive series expansions are unnecessary. Fresh validation directions and the supplied parameter-validation sets are still checked. A failed or unfinished certificate falls back to the existing calculation and never turns an unresolved result into PASS.

A retained factorization direction can be zero by ordinary identities even when its displayed expression is large. For a supported process with one massless external leg and at least three massive legs, the exact proof portfolio can first use a massive rest frame and a null momentum axis, then clear coordinate denominators and check the entire coherent spin polynomial. This is a generic external-kinematics identity proof with model parameters retained, rather than a test at a numerical phase-space point. It does not put an internal line on shell. The optional native arithmetic backend shares the existing stage deadline; if it is unavailable or cannot establish the certificate, the original direction remains available to the other proof and completion paths.

detail_sections.title: Reading the result
paragraphs: Use `"Output" -> "Details"` to inspect the candidate, fitted family, equations and independent validation. This is the appropriate output when an ordinary call returns `Failure`: it lets you distinguish an insufficient direction space, an unfixed coefficient, an unsupported check and a computation that reached its time limit.

Large expressions may be tested through a conservative upper bound on their high-energy power rather than an explicitly measured leading power. Such a report labels the quantity `"ObservedPowerUpperBound"`; it should not be read as an exact leading exponent. The report states which method completed.

The code can remove a retained direction after an exact identity certificate, but a few numerical zeros do not establish an identity. Unfinished proofs keep the direction. The same distinction applies when interpreting a successful sampled check of the final amplitude.

Defaults choose finite effort automatically. Set an integer `"RandomSeed"` to replay sampled kinematics, or adjust `"TimeConstraint"` for a longer calculation. A timeout remains visible in the result; it does not silently turn an undetermined family into a completed amplitude.

details: This is the main entry point when you want HEPCAT to carry out the complete constructive workflow. Supply an ordered all-ingoing process list, a diagram model and a factorization model. Routine calls need only those three arguments; the algorithm chooses its effort settings automatically.

Automatic effort estimates use the model's massive external spin states before diagrams are generated. Later stages measure the retained affine family and its directions, including a supplied correction basis, rather than only the displayed fixed expression. High-energy estimates also include the retained shell and reference expressions that can generate new correction directions, weighted by the full coherent-spin workload, before the stage clock is set. The limits remain finite, explicit settings stay authoritative and the overall construction clock still bounds every stage. Detailed output records the measurements used to choose the automatic settings.

Inside a high-energy fit, the already requested exact masses and couplings may be evaluated before the affine matrix and repeated-term catalog are expanded. The original amplitude and retained family remain symbolic outside that fitter. Each catalog receives a work-based scheduling estimate and a finite hard allowance within the same stage and overall clocks; all requested parameter assignments and independent validations remain required. This internal scheduling needs no additional user option.

The default `"PolePreference" -> "AllPhysical"` favors a final form whose denominator factors are physical propagators. Use `"PolePreference" -> "AllSpurious"` to favor admissible massless-reference forms instead, or `"Mixed"` to admit both. When no spurious reference is eligible for a leg, AllSpurious uses a physical replacement. Final expressions have no auxiliary Xi unless the caller explicitly chooses Xi, IndependentXi or None. Every result must still pass the same mandatory checks.

The diagram model supplies the interactions used by [CreateDiagrams](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/CreateDiagrams). The factorization model supplies complete lower-point amplitudes used by [FactorizationAmplitudeChannels](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/FactorizationAmplitudeChannels). They can be the same model at four points, but the factorization model must contain enough higher-point information for larger processes.

A successful ordinary call returns the final bare expression after all required checks pass. `"Output" -> "Amplitude"` instead returns `{externalMassRules, expression}`, which you can pass to [PrepareAmplitudes](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/PrepareAmplitudes) again. `"Output" -> "Details"` retains the stage results, timings, seed and validation report.

An explicit `"FeynmanModel"` also allows the wrapper to validate one fixed factorization or high-energy representative before proving every alternative in its retained affine family equivalent. Every standard check and the independent Feynman comparison must pass at all resolved independent validation parameter assignments. This is sampled validation of that expression, not a uniqueness proof or a change to the strict behavior of [CompleteHighEnergy](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/CompleteHighEnergy) on its own. Before these independent checks, a newly selected point receives ordinary final preparation through [PrepareAmplitudes](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/PrepareAmplitudes). An identical point already prepared in the same call is reused. The unused affine family remains available in Details; the simplification adds no internal-shell assumptions and uses no benchmark terms.

With that explicit independent benchmark, the wrapper can also propose a high-energy candidate after the first complete exact energy chart has been solved together with the actual physical-channel constraints. This is an early hypothesis: other energy directions and parameter assignments may remain unvisited, spurious and reference fit groups may remain unvisited, and unclassified correction coordinates remain recorded. The wrapper prepares the fixed hypothesis and checks every original physical channel, automatic spurious-pole cancellation, high-energy growth, reference independence and full Feynman agreement at all normal validation parameter assignments, including all three automatic assignments for the bundled SM. A failed, incomplete or opposite-sign comparison returns to strict completion in the original correction space. Neither one successful chart nor a rejected hypothesis removes a direction or discharges an unvisited obligation.

A separate recovery route applies when an automatic high-energy stage finishes its exact fit and proves every remaining direction zero, then reaches its deadline during independent validation. The wrapper may use the remaining overall budget for a separate visible stage, Validating retained HE candidate. Every original fit parameter assignment is rechecked with the normal held-out seeds and sample counts, including all physical poles, apparent spurious poles, high-energy growth and reference independence. The original child stays UNRESOLVED in Details. An explicit high-energy time limit, an unfinished coordinate classification or a known failed held-out check prevents this recovery. Only complete validation allows the ordinary final preparation and final checks to continue.

For a complete minimal massive fermion line with five or more same-helicity colorless vectors, the AllPhysical pole preference can combine emission subsets using ordinary Dirac and two-dimensional determinant identities. This keeps physical propagators off shell and uses the actual model vertices. The direct route currently requires an explicit FeynmanModel option and is selected only after every original physical channel, high-energy bound, reference check and Feynman comparison passes. Detailed output records a stage named Physical chiral current. Unsupported interactions or incomplete ordered-diagram sets continue through the ordinary completion workflow.

The final display reports the run seed, total time, [SpinorExpressionComplexity](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/SpinorExpressionComplexity) score and check table before returning the expression. Detailed output stores the same score as `"Complexity"`. If the bounded complexity measurement cannot finish, that entry is an explanatory Missing value; it is never replaced by a different size measure such as LeafCount.

For colored constructive processes, the function separates an exact independent SU(3) color basis and constructs each scalar spinor coefficient against the correspondingly projected channels. Every coefficient must pass the ordinary physical-pole, spurious-pole, high-energy and reference checks. The output is the full sum of color tensors times their validated coefficients. Details retain the basis, its interference matrix and the coefficient reports. [WriteSPINASProcess](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/WriteSPINASProcess) can export this full expression and compare its coherent color sum with CalcHEP and MadGraph. An explicit "FeynmanModel" also works for this colored route. Its independent diagrams are converted once and projected into a common exact color basis together with the constructive diagrams and original channels. The basis includes structures present only in the benchmark, so a missing color component cannot escape the comparison. Each coefficient retains the separate benchmark model and its parameter scope; the benchmark is used for validation, not as a construction source.

detail_sections.title: What happens during a construction
paragraphs: HEPCAT generates the diagrams and prepares their expressions, then builds the known factorization channels. [CompleteFactorization](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/CompleteFactorization) solves any physical residue deficits. The usual route then uses [CompleteHighEnergy](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/CompleteHighEnergy), prepares the completed expression with external identities and runs [CheckAmplitudes](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/CheckAmplitudes). When an explicit independent Feynman model is supplied, the wrapper can instead validate an already fixed representative as described below.

The stages pass more than their displayed expressions to one another. Original channel targets, discarded preparation remainders and remaining correction directions are retained. In particular, the final simplification does not apply diagram-local internal-shell conditions to the assembled amplitude.

The progress display names the current stage and shows both its elapsed time and the total time. At the end, the function prints the run seed, total time, final complexity score and check results before returning. `"ProgressReporting" -> False` and `"PrintReport" -> False` suppress those displays when running a script.

detail_sections.title: Checking one fixed representative
paragraphs: A factorization solve can leave an affine family: one particular expression plus free coefficients multiplying other expressions. Some of those directions may vanish by ordinary identities, but certifying every direction can take longer than checking the particular expression itself. With an explicit `"FeynmanModel"`, the wrapper may first try that fixed factorization point when free coordinates remain. It may also try a finite fixed candidate retained by an unresolved or underdetermined high-energy stage.

The high-energy stage has a second opportunity to propose a fixed point. Once one exact energy chart is complete, it can solve those rows together with the physical-channel constraints already obtained and use the resulting particular solution as a hypothesis. A complete chart covers its supported spin components at its own fixed-angle kinematics; the remaining fit charts, parameter assignments and unvisited spurious/reference fit groups are still obligations. Details preserve the original affine coordinates, every unclassified direction and the unvisited work. This proposal does not claim that the full fit or the full family is complete.

The wrapper first simplifies the hypothesis with ordinary external identities. Acceptance then requires [CheckAmplitudes](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/CheckAmplitudes) to pass the complete physical-channel report, automatic spurious-pole checks, the high-energy bound, reference independence and independent full-amplitude Feynman comparison. The checks run at every normal independent validation parameter assignment, including all three automatic assignments for the bundled SM, with the normal held-out seeds and sample counts. The first fit chart is not substituted for this validation.

The Feynman expression is generated once and reused only as a benchmark. It supplies no correction terms, fitted coefficients or replacement answer. The selected expression is the fixed constructive candidate that passed validation. Its unproved family directions are retained; they are not silently declared zero. These attempts share the existing construction clock.

If the hypothesis fails any check, returns an opposite sign or cannot finish validation, the wrapper continues strict completion from the original correction space and retained input when time remains. It does not continue from a first-chart restriction that has been mistaken for a complete solution. An incomplete attempt never becomes a passing result.

Request `"Output" -> "Details"` and inspect `"RepresentativeSelection"`. It records the source stage, retained family, free coordinates, validation reports and explicit `"UniquenessEstablished" -> False`. A successful selection means the chosen point passed the supported checks, not that every point in the family is equivalent or that the formula has received a generic analytic proof. The high-energy subreport also retains `"PointReadyCheckpoint"`, which identifies the completed chart and unvisited work. Its `"AllFitGroupsComplete" -> False` and `"FamilyUniquenessEstablished" -> False` describe the unfinished fit, even if the wrapper later accepts the separately validated fixed point.

Without an explicit `"FeynmanModel"`, the ordinary strict completion path is unchanged. Calling [CompleteHighEnergy](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/CompleteHighEnergy) directly also remains strict: genuine acceptable-growth contact freedom or unfinished identity proofs still produce an underdetermined or unresolved report. This wrapper policy does not infer an unknown contact interaction or prove that its coefficient vanishes.

detail_sections.title: Useful choices
paragraphs: `"PolePreference" -> "AllPhysical"` is the default. It favors a final representation with physical propagator denominators. `"AllSpurious"` favors admissible massless-reference denominators, while `"Mixed"` admits both. These choices guide preparation and completion; none weakens a mandatory check or promises a globally shortest expression. Details report whether the requested physical-only representation was achieved.

For four-point processes with reciprocal massless references, the constructor can repair uncanceled bracket poles with alternate diagram preparations. Ordinary final reduction cancels a removable bracket product even under this preference.

For a supported five-point process with three massless legs, the constructor tries compact reference choices related by exchange, or a complete sum of shifted factorization channels. It keeps a candidate only after checking the physical residues, spurious-pole cancellation, high-energy behavior, reference independence and any supplied Feynman comparison. Exchange symmetry is preserved by projection or verified by exact external identities.

With AllSpurious and an independent Feynman model, a complete line of cubic vector emissions from one massive fermion pair can be combined before individual diagram preparation. When one vector has the opposite helicity, the constructor tries shared external references and groups adjacent emission orders using external identities. It reads the masses and couplings from the diagram model and uses the Feynman model only for validation. If the attempt fails, ordinary construction continues.

A supported cubic vector line with several vectors of each helicity can instead use the ordinary off-shell Dirac numerator. The constructor chooses shared massless references, checks the complete result against the original factorization channels and independent Feynman model, and returns the validated expression without a separate compact-form search on this route.

With AllSpurious and an independent Feynman model, a supported tree with two massive Dirac fermion lines and two external massless vectors can combine the photon attachments on each line before contracting the currents. Both equal and opposite photon helicities are supported. The constructor reads the couplings, poles and exchange signs from the original diagrams, then checks the grouped result against the original factorization channels and the independent Feynman model. If the grouped candidate fails a check, construction continues along the other available routes.

For a supported six-fermion tree with two massless vector exchanges, AllSpurious can group the two orders of attachment on each central fermion line over their common vector propagators. There are no external photon references in this case, so the compact result uses physical propagators only. The grouped sum is built from the diagram model and returned early only after all ordinary checks and the independent Feynman comparison pass. If that attempt fails, the usual completion continues.

For four external vectors of the same helicity on a supported fermion line, AllSpurious can combine adjacent emission orders in pairs. For larger supported lines, it combines terminal pairs with memoized subsets of the remaining emissions. A two-dimensional momentum determinant collects repeated leading products, and external momentum conservation shortens the remaining insertions. The construction uses the supplied cubic vertices; it does not read a known final answer or add a new interaction. All propagators remain off shell in this route.

These same-helicity subset proposals use external massless reference spinors rather than leaving auxiliary Xi symbols. The existing bounded topology checks require the complete ordered cubic diagram inventory. An independent FeynmanModel is required, and every original physical channel, discovered spurious pole, high-energy bound, reference check and full-amplitude comparison must pass at both validation parameter assignments. Unsupported interactions, incomplete inventories and exhausted budgets continue through the ordinary completion workflow. A compact expression found this way is not a proof of absolute minimality.

For larger AllSpurious results with an independent Feynman model, the constructor can group terms by their compound physical poles. If the groups form a complete exchange orbit, it tries Schouten and an external momentum determinant to reduce one group, then uses exchange symmetry to propose the complete expression. The original validated result remains available if the proposal is unavailable, longer, or fails any check.

With a single massless leg there is no second massless external spinor to use as a reference. AllSpurious can therefore return a physical-only expression, with the auxiliary reference resolved. Use Xi, IndependentXi or None explicitly for workflows that retain auxiliary references.

Use `"FeynmanModel" -> feynmanModel` when you have an independent [FeynmanModel](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/FeynmanModel) for the same process and want a full-amplitude comparison as well. That model is a separate physical input and is not guessed from the constructive model.

`"Parallelization"` and `"MaxKernels"` control the use of local workers. `"TimeConstraint"` changes the overall budget. An integer `"RandomSeed"` replays the sampled kinematics; Automatic chooses and records a seed for the run. You do not need numerical parameter rules unless you want values different from those in the models.

detail_sections.title: If construction does not complete
paragraphs: A failed, opposite-sign or unresolved mandatory comparison prevents the ordinary call from returning an allegedly validated amplitude. An unfinished proof about the full affine family is a different issue: only an explicit independent Feynman model permits the separately checked fixed-point route above. Request `"Output" -> "Details"` to see which stage stopped, which representative was tried and why. A missing lower-point input, an insufficient correction space and an exhausted time limit require different remedies.

An independent Feynman comparison must use the same vertex and external-state convention as the constructive model. `Opp Sign` is useful diagnostic information, but it prevents a validated construction just like another failed check. Align conventions at the model level: an arbitrary sign change to one lower-point amplitude can alter relative signs when that amplitude is sewn into a higher-point channel. The bundled constructive SM vertices use the same charged-current sign as the unchanged CalcHEP model. No sign is fitted to a process or changed by the checker.

When you want to understand an intermediate expression, use the individual functions rather than increasing every resource option. Start with diagrams, inspect their prepared pairs, then examine factorization details. The tutorial on constructing an amplitude in stages shows that sequence and explains how to keep the information needed by the following stage.

Advanced stage options can be supplied through `"PreparationOptions"`, `"FactorizationOptions"`, `"HighEnergyOptions"`, `"FinalPreparationOptions"`, `"CheckOptions"` and their channel/Feynman counterparts. These are overrides for a specific investigation, not required setup for every calculation.
